name: better-ui
description: Design engineering principles for making interfaces feel polished. Use when building UI components, reviewing frontend code, implementing animations, hover states, shadows, borders, micro-interactions, enter/exit animations, or any visual detail work. Triggers on UI polish, design details, "make it feel better", "feels off", stagger animations, border radius, optical alignment, image outlines, box shadows.

name: better-accessibility
description: Accessibility engineering for product UI — focus, keyboard, ARIA, forms, and screen readers. Use when building or reviewing components, modals, menus, or fixing a11y issues.

name: better-colors
description: OKLCH color for the web — convert, generate palettes, check contrast, handle gamut, and theme with semantic tokens including dark mode.

name: better-interface
description: Holistic interface review that coordinates the better-* skills (a11y, layout, writing, typography, colors, UI) for a screen, flow, or product.

name: better-layout
description: Layout structure for web UI — grouping, alignment, reading order, progressive disclosure, breakpoints, and RTL-aware spacing.

name: better-typography
description: Web typography from font choice and type scale to wrapping, truncation, OpenType features, and readable measure.

name: better-writing
description: UX writing and interface copy — button labels, errors, empty states, placeholders, and voice/tone for product UI.

name: improve-ui
description: Audit an existing product surface against its own design evidence, identify verified UI problems, and write self-contained implementation plans for another agent without modifying product source.

name: improve-animations
description: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans. Read-only on source code - it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to improve animations, audit motion, make an app feel better, or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.

name: review-animations
description: Strict motion review of a diff against Emil's craft bar — justified motion, easing, duration, origin, GPU-only props, a11y. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

name: find-animation-opportunities
description: Search a UI for places that should animate — and reject what shouldn't. Read-only: proposes precise motion recipes, does not implement them.

name: animation-vocabulary
description: Turn a vague motion description into the exact term — "the bouncy popover thing" → Pop in — so you can prompt agents and designers with the right words.

name: apple-design
description: Apple's interface and fluid-motion principles from WWDC design talks, translated for the web — continuous gestures, rubber-banding, physical feel.

name: pick-ui-library
description: Opinionated library picker for common frontend tasks — toasts, cmdk, charts, DnD, OTP, motion — from Emil's trusted stack instead of AI inventing one.

name: impeccable
description: Flagship design skill for production-grade, anti-generic frontend interfaces with strong craft and consistency.

name: baseline-ui
description: Quickly deslop UI code by fixing spacing, hierarchy, typography, and small layout issues. Use when the interface needs a fast cleanup or polish pass.

name: emil-design-eng
description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, components, animation, and production-ready frontend craft.

name: polish
description: Final quality pass for spacing, alignment, and consistency to prepare UI for launch.

name: animate
description: Enhance UX with purposeful animation and micro-interactions that support usability and delight.

name: critique
description: Evaluate design quality with structured UX scoring, persona checks, and actionable remediation guidance.

name: make-interfaces-feel-better
description: Design engineering principles for making interfaces feel polished, with focus on micro-interactions, typography, and visual details.

name: ui-skills-root
description: Use when the user needs UI help and you must route by topic, stack, and intent to the smallest useful set of UI skills.

name: fixing-accessibility
description: Audit and fix HTML accessibility issues including ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast, and form errors. Use when adding interactive controls, forms, dialogs, or reviewing WCAG compliance.

name: fixing-motion-performance
description: Audit and fix animation performance issues including layout thrashing, compositor properties, scroll-linked motion, and blur effects. Use when animations stutter, transitions jank, or reviewing CSS/JS animation performance.

name: vocabulary
description: Precise design and UI vocabulary from index.how/to/articulate — reverse-lookup for typography, color, layout, motion, a11y, components, and more when you need the exact word.

name: grill-me
description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

name: grill-with-docs
description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADRs and glossary) as we go.

name: improve-codebase-architecture
description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when building features or fixing bugs test-first, or when you want red-green-refactor / integration tests.

name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
description: Configure a repo for Matt Pocock engineering skills — issue tracker, triage labels, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use.

name: triage
description: Move issues and external PRs through a triage state machine — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

name: ux-heuristics
description: Heuristic UX evaluation with Nielsen's 10 as the sole scorecard. Pair with ux-principles for Laws of UX and classic interaction principles.

name: interface-review
description: User-invoked interface review of uncommitted work, a branch, or a PR — classifies introduced vs regression vs pre-existing, then routes through better-interface.

name: create-design-md
description: Create or update a DESIGN.md from an existing product repo or public website — extract design language and tokens for coding agents without changing product source.

name: fixing-metadata
description: Audit and fix HTML metadata — titles, descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD, and robots directives.

name: animate
description: Build an animation from scratch in the order that determines whether it feels right — purpose, tool, properties, curve, interruptibility, exit — then write the implementation.

name: prototype
description: Build multiple genuinely different versions of a UI piece behind a visual picker so you can flip through them live and promote the one that feels right. Explicit invoke only.

name: ux-principles
description: UX principles review — Laws of UX (Fitts, Hick, Doherty, Peak-End, Gestalt, …) plus progressive disclosure, affordances, mapping, defaults, and forgiveness. Complements ux-heuristics.

name: transitions-dev
description: Production-ready CSS transitions for web apps from transitions.dev — badges, dropdowns, modals, page slides, toasts, skeletons, and more. Use when adding or auditing UI motion.

name: transitions-polish
description: Polish existing motion against transitions.dev motion tokens — duration, distance, scale, blur, easing, and open/close asymmetry. Add-on to transitions-dev.

name: animate-expo
description: Build React Native / Expo animations that feel right on device — Reanimated, Gesture Handler, sheets, haptics. For web motion use animate.

name: ask-sonner
description: Sonner toast library guide — Toaster setup, promise/loading toasts, styling, theming, positioning, and common troubleshooting.

name: mobile-native
description: Make web apps feel native on phones — sticky hover, 100vh, input zoom, tap lag, notch, PWA/touch fixes. For RN motion use animate-expo.

name: write-swift
description: Modern Swift craft — value types, Swift 6 concurrency, protocols/generics, API design, performance, Testing, and macros.

name: break
description: Render a component in every reachable state on a temporary page and stress-test it — visual report of what breaks under worst-case content.

name: explain-interface
description: Explain how something on the web was built — reverse-engineer layers and techniques from a live page or component without judging quality.

name: variant
description: Build multiple purposeful variants of a component behind a picker on the real page so you can iterate and choose a direction.

name: good-css
description: Opinionated modern CSS techniques for agents — adaptive declarations before breakpoints, CSS features before scripts. Works with plain CSS, Tailwind, StyleX, and more.

name: stageshow
description: Build faux product UI that looks real — stills, cursor demos, phones, dashboards, bento grids and marketing heroes in React and CSS.

name: agentation
description: Add the Agentation visual feedback toolbar to a Next.js project and wire it so browser feedback reaches the coding agent.

name: agentation-self-driving
description: Autonomous design critique via the Agentation toolbar — annotate a live page in a headed browser for UI review and self-driving feedback.

name: alignment
description: Measures a running page for edges, gaps, centring and radii that miss by a pixel or two, then judges visual weight and returns a numbered report with proof.

name: audit
description: Reviews a change, a session or a whole codebase against every skill in this collection and returns one ranked, numbered report.

name: avatar
description: Draws any object as a flat character with two capsule eyes, then animates its whole body so it glances, blinks, breathes, follows the pointer and falls asleep.

name: bots
description: Turns chosen Grok Bots into a shakeable pile, portfolio cards and an org chart page, each with a link to copy the bot, with private details stripped.

name: color
description: Holds text and control contrast to exact ratios, routes colour through role tokens and gives dark mode its own palette.

name: copy
description: Writes interface labels in Title Case, short and plain, with one-line descriptions and no em dashes.

name: deconstruct
description: Breaks an animation or interaction into a state machine and a timeline of every property, on a page you can scrub and edit.

name: defaults
description: Applies house defaults for scroll edges, surfaces, type, sound, focus, forms, loading, hotkeys and dialogs.

name: frames
description: Records a performance trace of one interaction on a throttled CPU, names what drops frames or delays input, then proves the fix with a second trace.

name: gather
description: Collects references from the user's own library, their boards and pattern sites onto one linked board before a design is built.

name: keyboard
description: Walks a running page with the keyboard alone, records every focus stop and reports controls it cannot reach, see or operate.

name: lab
description: Builds a temporary page that shows every variant and state of real components at once, each linked to its source.

name: match
description: Rebuilds a named reference from its real source and computed values, then compares the two side by side.

name: motion
description: Applies house motion for what animates, easing, durations, springs, gestures, exits and reduced motion.

name: prose
description: Writes posts and breakdowns that open on where the author stands, show the options that lost, give exact numbers and mark every guess as a guess.

name: prototype
description: Builds several real, labelled variants of one idea on a single page so the user can pick, then deletes the rest.

name: restraint
description: Ships the smallest thing that does the job and deletes what nobody asked for.

name: reuse
description: Reaches for the project's own components, then a maintained library, then a native feature, before writing new code.

name: rule
description: Turns a repeated correction into a short project rule with the broken and fixed line, then applies it to existing code.

name: scope
description: Changes exactly what was asked, keeps what already worked and finishes every item in the message.

name: ship
description: Commits, pushes, merges and releases a change, watches the checks and confirms it is live.

name: verify
description: Checks a change in the running app before calling it done, then says where to see it.

name: viewports
description: Renders a page at every width, each breakpoint edge, a short landscape phone and 200% text, then reports what overflows, clips or hides.

name: animation-performance
description: Keep web animations inside the frame budget — composite-only properties, main-thread cost, jank diagnosis. For easing/duration use animate; for craft review use review-animations.

name: break-ui
description: Stress-test UI with worst-case data (long names, missing fields, extreme counts) behind a Demo/Worst-case toggle and report every break with a fix.

name: remove-animations
description: Find animations the interface does not need and remove them — never adds or retunes motion. For places that should animate use find-animation-opportunities.
